prompt:
Draw exactly ONE new Small Seal font glyph from the attached reference image. The reference contains FOUR historical specimens of the SAME character, labelled THX, CCZ, QJZ, DYC. These are evidence for one character: use all four to understand its identity and stroke structure. Produce one new original coherent Gothic/monoline interpretation, informed by all four rather than tracing THX or any single specimen's brush silhouette. When forms disagree, choose a coherent attested WHOLE form; never splice incompatible alternative structures. Preserve the essential branches, counters, detachments, number and arrangement of components, and distinctive ancient character identity. Do not substitute a modern Chinese character.

Trace the real course of each stroke as a smooth centerline with rounded curves. Each stroke has exactly constant width throughout, approximately 4% of the full canvas width, with perfectly rounded caps and joins. No swelling, taper, serifs, brush texture, rough edges, pressure modulation, or pointed ends. Ensure the counters stay open and distinct strokes stay separated where the sources require it. Draw the glyph centered and occupying approximately the central 70% of a square canvas with generous clear margins, balanced spacing and a consistent sans-serif Gothic style.

Output exactly one glyph only, pure BLACK smooth monoline strokes on a fully TRANSPARENT background. No text, labels, chart, frame, grid, specimen copies, multiple alternatives, calligraphy, backdrop, shadows, or watermark.

Character U+3D03B. Essential structural reading aid, subordinate to the four specimens: Left ritual/altar component with detached upper dash, longer horizontal below attached to long center stem, and two separated side strokes. Right component has a top horizontal turning downward smoothly at far right into a long outside vertical stroke. A SECOND short horizontal sits detached just below the top horizontal inside the outer corner. Beneath it is a small U/cup-shaped form with two uprights and a crossbar between them, creating ONE enclosed lower counter with two tiny upward prongs above that crossbar. Keep a clear gap between the cup and the second horizontal above it. There must be no bottom outer enclosing horizontal.

visual_review.method: white-background inspection composite compared visually against THX, CCZ, QJZ, DYC
visual_review.notes: Compared all four specimens: left ritual component, outer top/right bent stroke, second horizontal and inner pronged cup with single counter retained, with gaps between components.
visual_review.confidence: draft visual comparison; not scholarly certification
